scope: Registered-land adverse possession and possessory-title procedures

official_sources.finding: Applications for adverse possession of registered land are made under section 4 of the Registration of Title Act 1964 and Rule 45, using LR Form 6; the applicant must prove the facts relied upon and each case is considered on its merits.
Tailte publishes Form 5 and Form 6 adverse-possession/possessory-title guidance and sample rulings.
The current catalogue lists LR Forms 4, 5, 6, 10 and later forms dealing with possessory title and adverse possession.

critical_distinctions: First registration with possessory title is distinct from an application concerning possession of already registered land.
Tailte's registered-land adverse-possession route expressly requires proof of facts; a bare assertion that the limitation period has expired is insufficient.
Possessory title is an evidential/title-class issue and must not be treated as identical to the underlying limitation claim.
Prescriptive easement claims are separate from title-by-adverse-possession claims.

2021_prescription_context.effect: The 2021 Act primarily reforms prescription of easements and profits à prendre and contains savers for pending proceedings/applications. It must not be automatically treated as a wholesale replacement of the statutory adverse-possession framework.

guardrails: No individual adverse-possession claim is assessed.
No ownership result is inferred from the existence of a form.
Official guidance is not substituted for the underlying statutory provisions.
